posts.text:
After the 1927 World Series, Lou Gehrig and Babe Ruth hit the road: Gehrig's Larrupin' Lous against Ruth's Bustin' Babes. This program is from their October 23, 1927 game in Oakland.

Explore his story with the Lou Gehrig Fan Club:
https://lougehrigfanclub.com
posts.alt_text: Souvenir program with a decorative border. It reads "Busting Babes vs. Larruping Lous" above a halftone photo of Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig in Yankees uniforms, each resting a hand on a bat, with "Oakland Baseball Park, Sunday, October 23, 1927" below.
posts.sources: The program itself (printed date and park); Baseball Hall of Fame collection and SABR accounts of the 1927 barnstorming tour.

posts.topic: Four home runs in one game, June 3, 1932
posts.text:
On June 3, 1932, Lou Gehrig hit four home runs in one game against the Philadelphia Athletics, the first player of the 20th century to do it.

Explore his story with the Lou Gehrig Fan Club:
https://lougehrigfanclub.com
posts.alt_text: Black-and-white photo of four baseball players standing side by side in a ballpark. The two in the middle wear Yankees jerseys and the two on the ends wear jerseys with a large "A". The third player from the left holds a glove.
posts.sources: SABR game project, June 3, 1932; Baseball Hall of Fame, Lou Gehrig hits four consecutive home runs.

posts.text:

posts.text:
On July 4, 1939, the Yankees retired Lou Gehrig's number 4, the first uniform number retired in major league baseball.

Explore his story with the Lou Gehrig Fan Club:
